name: slack-gif-creator
headline: Autotab-Starter: Automate Browser Tasks with AI
short_description: Autotab-starter enables users to create browser agents that automate real-world tasks seamlessly. Ideal for enhancing productivity and efficiency, this Python-based tool simplifies automation in various applications.
author: Planetary-Computers

sections.overview:
Autotab-starter is a Python-based framework for creating browser agents that automate real-world tasks across web applications. Built by Planetary Computers, it provides developers with tools to build automation scripts that interact with web interfaces programmatically. The framework includes support for credential management, browser mirroring capabilities, and configurable parameters through YAML configuration files. It's designed for developers who need to automate repetitive web-based workflows while maintaining control over browser interactions. The tool simplifies the creation of reliable automation without requiring manual task execution.
Automate data entry in web forms to save time and reduce errors.
Scrape data from websites for analysis or reporting purposes.
Schedule and manage online tasks to enhance personal productivity.
Perform repetitive browser actions, such as clicking buttons or filling forms.
sections.usage:
```
Create a browser agent using autotab-starter to automate [SPECIFIC_TASK] in [TARGET_APPLICATION]. The agent should perform the following steps: [LIST_STEPS]. Configure it to run on a schedule or trigger based on [CONDITION]. Include error handling for [COMMON_FAILURES].
```
Copy

```
```python
from autotab_starter import BrowserAgent

# Define the automation task
agent = BrowserAgent(
    name="SaaS_License_Tracker",
    description="Automates monthly SaaS license renewal tracking in Productiv"
)

# Configure the automation steps
agent.add_step(
    action="navigate",
    target="https://app.productiv.com/licenses",
    wait_for="table.loaded"
)
agent.add_step(
    action="extract",
    selector=".license-table tbody tr",
    output="licenses"
)
agent.add_step(
    action="filter",
    condition="expiry_date <= today + 30 days",
    output="upcoming_renewals"
)
agent.add_step(
    action="email",
    recipients=["finance@company.com"],
    subject="Upcoming SaaS Renewals",
    body="The following licenses expire within 30 days:\n{upcoming_renewals}"
)

# Run the agent
agent.run()

# Expected output:
# [
#   {"name": "Slack", "expiry_date": "2023-11-15", "cost": "$120/month"},
#   {"name": "Notion", "expiry_date": "2023-11-20", "cost": "$8/month"}
# ]
# Email sent to finance@company.com with renewal details.
```
```
